advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a failed/empty store-wide position map degrades to per-TICKET map building (not per-event under-lock walks): pass None on failure, or make `_build_authorship_ledger` rebuild a per-ticket map when the supplied map is empty.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:114 `if position_commits is None:` — only None triggers the per-ticket map build; an empty dict does not
src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:144-151 map miss falls to `resolve_event_commit(position_str, ticket_dir, ...)` per event, inside the locked section
src/rebar/_commands/compact.py:427 docstring claims 'an empty map simply restores the per-ticket behaviour' — it does not; it yields per-EVENT resolution
advisory.finding: When the store-wide position map cannot be built (git failure), `_sweep_position_map` returns an empty dict `{}` which `_run_sweep` threads into every fold. Because `_build_authorship_ledger` only rebuilds a per-ticket map when `position_commits is None`, a non-None empty dict skips that build and every signed event falls back to `resolve_event_commit` PER EVENT while holding the store write lock — the exact per-event under-lock walk the change (and bug 7084) set out to eliminate, and worse than the pre-fix per-ticket walk.
scenarios: A git failure (timeout on a very large history, transient error) makes build_position_commit_map return {} during a sweep of thousands of tickets
advisory.suggested_fix: Have `_sweep_position_map` signal 'no prebuilt map' as `None` on failure (and let `_run_sweep` pass `None` through), OR change the `_build_authorship_ledger` guard to `if not position_commits:` so an empty map also triggers the per-ticket build.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the store-wide map build fails/returns empty and assert the sweep still does not perform per-event history resolution inside the lock.
evidence: tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_perf.py:test_a_sweep_walks_history_once_regardless_of_ticket_count asserts sweep_map==1 and per_event==0 only on the success path
ABSENCE: no test monkeypatches build_position_commit_map to return {} (or raise) to assert the degraded path still avoids per-event walks under the lock
advisory.finding: The per-sweep degraded path is untested: the perf tests assert the happy path (map built once, no fallback) but there is no test exercising `_sweep_position_map` returning `{}` and confirming folds do NOT collapse to per-event walks under the lock.
scenarios: Regression where the empty-map degradation reintroduces per-event walks would pass all current tests

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive assertion that the swept ticket's SNAPSHOT is present in the compaction commit (`git show --name-only HEAD`), alongside the existing negative stray-exclusion check.
evidence: assert stray.exists(), "the bystander's file must be left alone, not consumed"
compact.py `_commit_backfill`: `if _git(tracker, "diff", "--cached", "--quiet").returncode == 0: ... return` — a no-op staging makes no commit, leaving HEAD at the fixture commit
ABSENCE: no assertion that the swept ticket's `*-SNAPSHOT.json` appears in `git show --name-only HEAD`, so a regression staging the wrong/no dir goes undetected
advisory.finding: test_the_sweep_commit_does_not_steal_a_concurrent_writers_event asserts only that the stray file is absent from HEAD, never that the legitimately-folded ticket's SNAPSHOT was committed. If the new scoped staging (`git add -- {tid}/`) stages the wrong directory or nothing for the swept ticket, `_commit_backfill` reaches `git diff --cached --quiet`==0, makes no commit, and HEAD remains the fixture commit — so `stray.name not in committed` passes vacuously. The positive staging path of the `folded_ids` change is unverified.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the sweep, assert a `*-SNAPSHOT.json` under `_tdir(repo, tid)` (the swept ticket) IS in `committed`, e.g. `assert any(tid in line and 'SNAPSHOT' in line for line in committed.splitlines())`, so the scoped-staging path's positive behavior is verified, not just the bystander exclusion.
